key_insight: Treat user actions as camera-pose changes and use camera pose as a unified geometric conditioning signal for an autoregressive video model, enabling precise action control and long-horizon 3D-consistent generations.
problem_solved: Existing interactive world models treat actions as abstract controls and suffer from imprecise action execution and accumulated 3D inconsistency (visual drift) over long rollouts; this work resolves that by explicitly coupling actions to camera geometry.
method: Represent actions as relative camera-pose transforms and accumulate them into a global pose trajectory that conditions generation.
Use an autoregressive video diffusion / transformer model that synthesizes next frames conditioned on past frames and the current/target camera poses to enforce geometric consistency.
Train with multi-view/pose supervision and consistency losses (pose-conditioned rendering and temporal coherence) to reduce drift and enable long-horizon interactive rollouts.
impact: Provides a practical recipe for building controllable, long-horizon interactive 3D gaming worlds and simulators where user inputs map directly to reliable camera motions—useful for game development, virtual environments, and downstream research in embodied AI.
visual_elements: Diagram: pipeline showing user action → camera-pose delta → pose accumulator → autoregressive frame generator

paper_title: WorldCam: Interactive Autoregressive 3D Gaming Worlds with Camera Pose as a Unifying Geometric Representation
paper_authors: Jisu Nam, Yicong Hong, Chun-Hao Paul Huang, Feng Liu, JoungBin Lee
